prompt_text: I need braces or Invisalign in Columbus. Which specific orthodontists should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best orthodontist in Columbus Ohio for braces or Invisalign?
competitors_mentioned: Ohio State University College of Dentistry
answer_verbatim:
Quick question before I make specific recommendations: do you mean Columbus, Ohio (the most common), or a different Columbus? Also, do you prefer Invisalign (clear aligners) or traditional braces, and is this for an adult or a child/teen? Any insurance or budget constraints I should know about?

If you want me to pull up specific names/phones/addresses, tell me your ZIP code or the Columbus neighborhood you’d prefer (north/short north/downtown/east/south). I can then list 4–6 nearby orthodontists to call and why each is a good fit.

Meanwhile, here’s exactly how to find the best local orthodontists and what to ask when you call so you’ll quickly identify the right practice.

Which offices to prioritize calling (and why)
- Board-certified orthodontists. Board certification (American Board of Orthodontics) shows extra testing and a higher standard of training. Prioritize offices that list board-certified doctors.
- High-volume Invisalign providers (Platinum/Diamond). If you want Invisalign, call providers who are Platinum/Diamond — they treat many cases and will be more experienced with complex aligner movements.
- University orthodontic clinic (Ohio State University College of Dentistry, if you’re in Columbus, OH). Good for complex cases and lower-cost care supervised by faculty.
- Practices that advertise digital scanning (iTero), 3D planning, and clear retention options — those technologies tend to give faster, more predictable results.
- Practices with strong online reviews and transparent pricing/financing.

How to find specific offices fast
- Use the American Association of Orthodontists “Find an Orthodontist” tool (aaoinfo.org/find) to filter for board certification and location.
- Use the Invisalign “Find a Doctor” tool (invisalign.com/find-a-doctor) to locate Diamond/Platinum providers near you.
- Check Google Maps & Yelp for patient reviews and photos of before/after results.
- If cost is a major factor, check the university clinic (Ohio State U. Orthodontics in Columbus, OH).

What to ask when you call (short checklist)
- Do you do Invisalign? If so, what is your provider level (Premier/Gold/Platinum/Diamond)?
- Are you board certified (American Board of Orthodontics)?
- Do you offer a free or low-cost consultation and a written treatment plan with an estimate?
- What is your typical treatment length for cases like mine (crowding, gaps, bite correction)?
- Do you use digital scanning (iTero) instead of impressions?
- What are your payment/financing options and do you accept my insurance?
- Who does the regular adjustments—doctor or assistant—and how often are visits?
- What kind of retainers do you provide and is post-treatment care included?
- If I get braces, what options do you offer (metal, ceramic, self-ligating, lingual)?
- How do you handle emergencies after hours?

Sample 20–30 second call script
“Hi — I’m calling about orthodontic treatment. Do you do Invisalign or braces? Is the doctor board-certified, and do you offer a free consultation with a treatment plan estimate? I’m also interested in whether you use a digital scanner and what payment options you offer.”

If you want, I can:
- Look up specific orthodontists in Columbus (OH) near your ZIP and list 4–6 names with phone numbers, addresses, and why each might be a good fit.
- Or if you already prefer Invisalign vs braces, I can return only top Invisalign Diamond/Platinum providers near you.

Which would you like me to do?
